definitionEn: a place where doctors treat people who are very ill or injured
example: They took him to hospital after the crash.

definitionEn: a large room in a hospital with several beds
example: She is in the children's ward.

definitionEn: a doctor's office; also an operation
example: The GP surgery opens at eight.

definitionEn: the hospital department for sudden serious problems
example: Go to A&E if the bleeding does not stop.

definitionEn: when a surgeon cuts the body to repair something
example: He needs an operation on his knee.

definitionEn: a doctor who does operations
example: The surgeon explained the risks.

definitionEn: medicine put into the body with a needle
example: The injection did not hurt much.

definitionEn: a small solid piece of medicine you swallow
example: Take one tablet after food.

definitionEn: a substance you take to get better
example: This medicine tastes bitter.

definitionEn: liquid medicine you put in your eyes or nose
example: Use the drops three times a day.

definitionEn: a thick cream you put on the skin
example: Put ointment on the rash twice a day.

definitionEn: not healthy; feeling unwell
example: She is too ill to go to school.

definitionEn: ill; also feeling as if you might vomit
example: I was sick all night after the seafood.

definitionEn: a serious illness, often with a name
example: Measles is a disease you can prevent.

definitionEn: an illness caused by bacteria or a virus
example: The cut got an infection.

definitionEn: a tiny thing that can make you ill
example: A virus caused her high temperature.

definitionEn: tiny living things; some cause infection
example: Wash your hands to kill bacteria.

definitionEn: a change in the body that shows you are ill
example: A high temperature is a symptom of flu.

definitionEn: a body temperature that is too high because you are ill
example: She had a fever and stayed in bed.

definitionEn: to suddenly blow air from your nose
example: Cover your mouth when you sneeze.

definitionEn: a continuous pain that is not sharp
example: I have an ache in my back after PE.

definitionEn: an unpleasant feeling when something is wrong in the body
example: The pain in my ear is worse at night.

definitionEn: to lose blood from a cut
example: Press the cut if it continues to bleed.

definitionEn: an injury where the skin is broken
example: Keep the wound clean and dry.

definitionEn: an injury when you twist a joint too far
example: A sprain of the ankle needs rest.

definitionEn: to become larger because of injury or illness
example: His knee began to swell after the fall.

definitionEn: an uncomfortable feeling that makes you want to scratch
example: Mosquito bites itch for days.

definitionEn: red spots or patches on the skin
example: The rash appeared after the strawberries.

definitionEn: an illness that makes it hard to breathe
example: He uses an inhaler because of asthma.

definitionEn: a small device that sends medicine into the lungs
example: Keep your inhaler in your bag.

definitionEn: an illness where the body cannot control sugar in the blood
example: People with diabetes must be careful with sweets.

definitionEn: sneezing and itchy eyes caused by pollen
example: Hay fever is worse in May.

definitionEn: illness from eating bad or dirty food
example: Food poisoning kept him in bed for two days.

definitionEn: red, painful skin after too much sun
example: Sunburn can happen even on a cloudy day.

definitionEn: an injury from heat or fire
example: Cool the burn under cold water.

definitionEn: to become unconscious for a short time
example: She might faint if she does not eat breakfast.

definitionEn: not awake and not able to respond
example: He was unconscious for a few seconds after the hit.

definitionEn: awake and able to understand what is happening
example: Is the injured person still conscious?

definitionEn: to take air in and out of your lungs
example: Sit down and breathe slowly.

definitionEn: the beat of blood that you can feel in your wrist or neck
example: The nurse checked my pulse.

definitionEn: the force of blood as it moves through the body
example: Grandad has high blood pressure.

definitionEn: a picture of bones inside the body
example: The X-ray showed a crack in the wrist.

definitionEn: sticks you put under your arms to help you walk
example: He used crutches for six weeks.

definitionEn: a chair with wheels for people who cannot walk
example: The museum has a wheelchair at the entrance.

definitionEn: a cloth that holds an injured arm against the body
example: Her arm is in a sling.

definitionEn: thread used to close a deep cut
example: The doctor put in five stitches.

definitionEn: a hard covering that keeps a broken bone still
example: He wrote names on my plaster cast.

definitionEn: a cold bag you put on a swelling
example: Put an ice pack on the bruise.

definitionEn: an instrument that measures body temperature
example: The thermometer showed 39 degrees.

definitionEn: the instrument a doctor uses to listen to your heart and lungs
example: The doctor put the stethoscope on my back.

definitionEn: a list of people who must wait for treatment
example: There is a long waiting list for the specialist.

definitionEn: a doctor who knows a lot about one part of the body
example: You need a specialist for that knee.

definitionEn: a person who tests your eyesight
example: The optometrist said I need glasses.

definitionEn: lenses in a frame that help you see better
example: I cannot read the board without glasses.

definitionEn: small lenses you put on your eyes instead of glasses
example: Contact lenses are useful for sport.

definitionEn: a small device that helps you hear
example: Grandma wears a hearing aid in her right ear.

definitionEn: having a condition that makes some activities harder
example: The building is not easy for disabled visitors.

definitionEn: a larger toilet with extra space and support
example: The disabled toilet is on the ground floor.

definitionEn: how well your mind and feelings are
example: Talking to someone can help your mental health.

definitionEn: worry and pressure that can make you feel ill
example: Too much stress before exams is unhealthy.

definitionEn: worried and nervous, often for a long time
example: He feels anxious before every oral exam.

definitionEn: very sad for a long time and unable to enjoy things
example: If you feel depressed, tell an adult you trust.

definitionEn: when you cannot sleep well for many nights
example: Insomnia makes the next day at school hard.

definitionEn: extremely tired
example: I was exhausted after the night bus.

definitionEn: time when you are not active so the body can recover
example: You need rest, not another training session.

definitionEn: the food you usually eat; also eating less to lose weight
example: A balanced diet includes vegetables every day.

definitionEn: very overweight in a way that is bad for health
example: Doctors worry when a child is obese.

definitionEn: weighing less than is healthy
example: She looks underweight after the illness.

definitionEn: to become healthier and stronger through exercise
example: I want to get fit before the sports day.

definitionEn: when you cannot stop a harmful habit
example: Smoking can become an addiction.

definitionEn: breathing in smoke from cigarettes
example: Smoking is banned in school.

definitionEn: to stop using cigarettes
example: Dad wants to give up smoking this year.

definitionEn: drinks such as beer or wine that can make you drunk
example: Alcohol is not allowed at the school disco.

definitionEn: having had too much alcohol
example: It is dangerous to get drunk and walk home alone.

definitionEn: illegal substances, or medicine in some contexts
example: Say no if someone offers you drugs.

definitionEn: keeping yourself and things clean to stay healthy
example: Good hygiene means washing your hands before meals.

definitionEn: to clean your hands with soap and water
example: Wash your hands after you use the toilet.

definitionEn: to pull a brush through your hair
example: Brush your hair before the school photo.

definitionEn: when a dentist repairs a hole in a tooth
example: The dentist will fill a tooth on Monday.

definitionEn: wires that a dentist uses to straighten teeth
example: Braces are uncomfortable for the first week.

definitionEn: the special chair you sit in at the dentist
example: I hate sitting in the dentist chair.

definitionEn: when a nurse takes blood to check your health
example: You need a blood test before the operation.

definitionEn: a paper from a parent or doctor that explains an absence
example: Bring a sick note on Monday.

definitionEn: to rest in bed because you are ill
example: Stay in bed if you have a high temperature.

definitionEn: to use a thermometer to see if you have a fever
example: Mum will take your temperature after supper.

definitionEn: to phone emergency services for a vehicle to hospital
example: Call an ambulance if he cannot breathe.

definitionEn: the phone number you call for police, fire or ambulance
example: 112 is the emergency number in Poland.

definitionEn: a box of plasters, bandages and basic medical things
example: There is a first-aid kit in the staff room.

definitionEn: an unwanted result of taking medicine
example: Sleepiness is a side effect of this tablet.

definitionEn: the amount of medicine you should take at one time
example: Do not take a bigger dose than the label says.

definitionEn: something you say or write to a person who is ill
example: The class sent a card that said get well soon.
